---
title: "Use Cases"
---

Seven situations tether is built for, told as one story: each section starts
where the previous one left the dataset, and ends with `jj log` so you can
see what it did to the repository's history and bookmarks. The dataset is the
one the other guides use -- an Icechunk store `zarr/imaging`, a Neon database
`db/metrics`, a Lance table `features`, a directory of raw files `raw/plate1`,
and the analysis code repository `code` -- and each section ends with the
guide that explains the mechanics.

The `jj log` output is trimmed to change id, commit id, bookmarks, and
description; `@` is this checkout's working copy, `◆` the root. Under git,
read a bookmark as a branch and `@` as `HEAD`.

## 0. Set up

```bash
jj git init analysis && cd analysis            # or: git init analysis
tether init
tether add zarr/imaging --kind icechunk s3://bucket/imaging.icechunk --branch main
tether add db/metrics   --kind neon --project-id prj-123 --database neondb --role runner
tether add features     --kind lance s3://bucket/features.lance
tether add raw/plate1   --kind file s3://bucket/raw/plate1/
tether add code         --kind git ../analysis-code --remote origin
```

Nothing has been contacted yet. What the VCS sees is a handful of small TOML
files -- the config and one manifest per object -- and a `main` bookmark that
`init` put on the working copy, because `main` is the trunk: the bookmark that
stands for every object's own `main`.

```bash
jj status
```

```
Working copy changes:
A .tether/.gitignore
A .tether/objects/code.toml
A .tether/objects/db/metrics.toml
A .tether/objects/features.toml
A .tether/objects/raw/plate1.toml
A .tether/objects/zarr/imaging.toml
A tether.toml
Working copy  (@) : kmpvtnwq 4f1a2b3c main | (no description set)
Parent commit (@-): zzzzzzzz 00000000 (empty) (no description set)
```

`.tether/workspace.toml` and `.tether/ops.jsonl` are not listed: they are
per-checkout state, ignored by the `.gitignore` that `init` wrote.

## 1. Reproduce an analysis months later

*The report is out. Someone asks how a number was computed. The code is in
git; the data it read has moved on three times since.*

Commit the inputs next to the code that read them:

```bash
tether commit -m "Inputs for the Q3 report"
```

```
  pinned code -> tether.0a1b2c3d.f01a9d3c2b7ee5f6
  pinned db/metrics -> tether.0a1b2c3d.a91f0e2b77c3e5f6
  pinned features -> tether.0a1b2c3d.9e7c4b2f0a61e5f6
  pinned zarr/imaging -> tether.0a1b2c3d.6674305d5e1fe5f6
  recorded raw/plate1 (not recoverable)
committed 8d5719841a09
```

That commit holds the manifests -- one file per object naming the pin -- and
sits in the same history as `make_report.py`. Months later, from any clone:

```bash
TETHER_REV=8d5719841a09 python make_report.py      # every repo.open() resolves at that commit's pins
tether open zarr/imaging --rev 8d5719841a09         # s3://bucket/imaging.icechunk#tether.0a1b2c3d.6674305d5e1fe5f6
```

```python
from tether import Repo

repo = Repo.find(".")
h = repo.open("zarr/imaging", rev="8d5719841a09")   # read-only, at the pinned snapshot
```

And in CI, so you find out the day a pin stops resolving rather than the day
you need it:

```bash
tether verify --all-history        # exit 1 on any missing or drifted pin
```

What tether guaranteed: the Icechunk tag, the Neon branch, the Lance tag, and
the git tag are native refs that their systems will not expire or garbage
collect; the raw prefix was *recorded* (size, count, etag digest) and `verify`
reports whether it still matches, but files cannot be pinned -- the line says
so at commit time.

This commit was made on the trunk bookmark, `main`, where each object's
working ref is its own `main`: the inputs are whatever those branches held.
The commit moved the bookmark with it, and jj opened a fresh empty working
copy on top, as `jj commit` would:

```bash
jj log
```

```
@  xtqmwlkn 3c0dfe12 (empty) (no description set)
○  kmpvtnwq 8d571984 main | Inputs for the Q3 report
◆  zzzzzzzz 00000000
```

Read next: [Pinning](03-pinning.qmd).

## 2. Reprocess on a branch, then land it or throw it away

*A new model should relabel the imaging store and rewrite the metrics table.
Production readers must not see a half-done state, and the attempt may fail.*

```bash
tether new -b relabel-v3
```

```
on bookmark relabel-v3; working refs set up
  code          -> tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.relabel-v3  (created on first writable open)
  db/metrics    -> tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.relabel-v3  (created on first writable open)
  features      -> tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.relabel-v3  (created on first writable open)
  zarr/imaging  -> tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.relabel-v3  (created on first writable open)
```

A `relabel-v3` bookmark now sits where `main` is, and every system will get a
branch of the same name. Nothing was created yet: the job opens what it
writes, and the branch for that object appears in its system at that moment,
forked from the pin:

```python
repo = Repo.find(".")
h = repo.open("zarr/imaging", read_only=False)   # the Icechunk branch is created now
...                                               # write through h.session, then h.session.commit(...)
```

`main` -- the bookmark and every system's branch -- is untouched throughout.
When the job is done, commit pins the branches and moves `relabel-v3`:

```bash
tether commit -m "Relabel plate1 with model v3"
tether diff main --content
```

```
   modified  db/metrics  [3 tables changed]
                    modified  public.metrics  +1200 rows, -1200 rows
   modified  zarr/imaging  [2 arrays changed, 148 chunks]
                    modified  labels/0.0.0
                    modified  labels/0.0.1
                    ... 146 more (use --limit)
```

```bash
jj log
```

```
@  pmwzlkro 9a4e17b0 (empty) (no description set)
○  rzpkxwvn 41c0d9e2 relabel-v3 | Relabel plate1 with model v3
○  kmpvtnwq 8d571984 main | Inputs for the Q3 report
◆  zzzzzzzz 00000000
```

The bookmark moved; `main` did not. Two endings. Land it:

```bash
tether promote
```

```
  fast-forwarded zarr/imaging -> {'snapshot_id': 'Q7ZK2M9A1B7C8D4E'}
  fast-forwarded features -> {'branch': 'main', 'version': 42}
  fast-forwarded code -> {'sha': '9e1c3a0b...'}
  refused        db/metrics: Neon cannot promote a child branch into its parent; work on the trunk bookmark for databases that must receive writes on main, or copy the data with pg_dump/psql
```

Icechunk, Lance, and git upstream branches moved to the bookmark's branches
because nothing else had touched them since the fork point (a fast-forward).
Neon refuses -- there is no way to move `main` onto a child branch -- and says
what to do instead: run that job on the trunk bookmark so it writes `main`
directly, or copy the rows across. That refusal is the honest answer, not a
bug; because of it the trunk bookmark did not move (everything must land for
`main` to point at the commit). Finish the Neon half by hand on the trunk and
commit there. Pins are content-addressed, so the three objects that
fast-forwarded get the very pin ids `relabel-v3`'s commit made -- nothing new
is created in those stores -- and only the database gets a new one:

```bash
tether new main
pg_dump "$(tether open db/metrics --rev relabel-v3)" | psql "$(tether open db/metrics)"
tether commit -m "Metrics rewritten for model v3"
```

```
  pinned code -> tether.0a1b2c3d.9e1c3a0b7d2fe5f6
  pinned db/metrics -> tether.0a1b2c3d.55e2ab7d9c10e5f6
  pinned features -> tether.0a1b2c3d.3b7f2e9d0c41e5f6
  pinned zarr/imaging -> tether.0a1b2c3d.deb4861eb388e5f6
committed 7f3a2c1d0e5b
```

```bash
jj log
```

```
@  swqnlvtk d81c9f02 (empty) (no description set)
○  wknmqzlt 7f3a2c1d main | Metrics rewritten for model v3
│ ○  rzpkxwvn 41c0d9e2 relabel-v3 | Relabel plate1 with model v3
├─╯
○  kmpvtnwq 8d571984 Inputs for the Q3 report
◆  zzzzzzzz 00000000
```

Two lines of history describe the same states now, and the bookmark has done
its job. Drop the commit and the bookmark; `gc` deletes the branches because
their heads are pinned (by `main`'s commit, which names the same pins):

```bash
tether abandon relabel-v3         # the commit; nothing to unpin, main's commit names the same pins
jj bookmark delete relabel-v3     # the bookmark (tether abandon moved it to the parent)
tether gc --prune-bookmarks --no-dry-run
```

```
abandoned 41c0d9e2b7f3
deleted 4 branch(es)
  deleted  code: tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.relabel-v3  bookmark relabel-v3 (gone); head is pinned
  deleted  db/metrics: tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.relabel-v3  bookmark relabel-v3 (gone); head is pinned
  deleted  features: tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.relabel-v3  bookmark relabel-v3 (gone); head is pinned
  deleted  zarr/imaging: tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.relabel-v3  bookmark relabel-v3 (gone); head is pinned
```

```bash
jj log
```

```
@  swqnlvtk d81c9f02 (empty) (no description set)
○  wknmqzlt 7f3a2c1d main | Metrics rewritten for model v3
○  kmpvtnwq 8d571984 Inputs for the Q3 report
◆  zzzzzzzz 00000000
```

The other ending -- the attempt failed -- is the same three commands without
the trunk commit in between: `tether abandon relabel-v3 --gc` releases the
pins only it made, `jj bookmark delete` drops the name, and `gc
--prune-bookmarks` deletes a branch only when its head is pinned or nothing
was written to it; the attempt's unpinned writes are kept until you pass
`--force-prune`. That is the guard against losing an afternoon.

::: {.callout-note title="Rehearsing a database migration"}
The same flow rehearses a schema change: `tether new -b migration`, run it
against the Neon branch's URL, run the test suite, `tether diff main --content`
to see the row counts move. Landing it is the trunk recipe above or applying
the migration to `main` yourself; the branch was the rehearsal.
:::

Read next: [Branching and Writing](04-branching-and-writing.qmd).

## 3. A/B: two candidates, keep one

*Two labeling approaches. Run both against the same inputs, compare, promote
the winner, and leave nothing of the loser behind.*

Each candidate is a bookmark -- `a` and `b` -- and each bookmark is a branch
of the same name in every system, so the two never share a branch anywhere.
Run them side by side from two checkouts (a jj workspace or a git worktree
each). Left is A, right is B; each column is one shell.

**Set up.** B's checkout is created from A's; each starts its own bookmark.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="49%"}
**A** -- `analysis/`

```bash
jj workspace add ../analysis-b    # git: git worktree add ../analysis-b main
tether new -b a
```

```
on bookmark a; working refs set up
  ...  -> tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.a
```
:::
::: {.column width="2%"}
:::
::: {.column width="49%"}
**B** -- `analysis-b/`

```bash
cd ../analysis-b
tether new -b b
```

```
on bookmark b; working refs set up
  ...  -> tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.b
```
:::
::::

**Run and commit.** Each job labels the imaging store and rewrites the
feature scores through its own handles; each `commit` pins its bookmark's
branches, lands a dataset commit in the VCS, and moves the bookmark onto it.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="49%"}
```bash
python label.py --candidate a
tether commit -m "Labels: candidate A"
```

```
  pinned zarr/imaging -> tether.0a1b2c3d.b7e1...
  pinned features -> tether.0a1b2c3d.2d9f...
committed 5a1e9c0d7b2f
```
:::
::: {.column width="2%"}
:::
::: {.column width="49%"}
```bash
python label.py --candidate b
tether commit -m "Labels: candidate B"
```

```
  pinned zarr/imaging -> tether.0a1b2c3d.9c3a...
  pinned features -> tether.0a1b2c3d.71d4...
committed c4d82f1a6e93
```
:::
::::

Two bookmarks, two lines of history, one fork point -- and the same shape in
Icechunk and Lance, where `tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.a` and `tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.b`
both branch off the pin at `main`. B's working copy shows as `analysis-b@`:

```bash
jj log
```

```
@  ozxwmqtn e7b2c4a1 (empty) (no description set)
○  vmnzstyq 5a1e9c0d a | Labels: candidate A
│ ○  lwqrtxsu 3f9d0e6b analysis-b@ (empty) (no description set)
│ ○  qwrlkupt c4d82f1a b | Labels: candidate B
├─╯
○  wknmqzlt 7f3a2c1d main | Metrics rewritten for model v3
○  kmpvtnwq 8d571984 Inputs for the Q3 report
◆  zzzzzzzz 00000000
```

**Compare** -- from either checkout, as datasets rather than directories:

```bash
tether diff a b --content
```

```
   modified  zarr/imaging  [1 array changed, 148 chunks]
                    modified  labels/0.0.0
                    ...
   modified  features  [3 fragments added, 3 removed]
```

**Land A.** One command from A: `promote` moves each system's `main` onto
`a`'s branch (a fast-forward: `main` had not moved since the fork) and then
moves the `main` bookmark onto A's dataset commit.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="49%"}
```bash
tether promote
```

```
  fast-forwarded zarr/imaging -> {'snapshot_id': 'Q7ZK...'}
  fast-forwarded features -> {'branch': 'main', 'version': 42}
main -> 5a1e9c0d7b2f
```
:::
::: {.column width="2%"}
:::
::: {.column width="49%"}
B is untouched by this: its bookmark and branches are its own. If B's
checkout later moves onto the new `main` (`jj new main`), `tether status`
says the working copy left bookmark `b` and how to return; `tether new b`
returns, and a bookmark whose pins the dataset no longer names is re-forked
(refused while it holds uncommitted writes).
:::
::::

**Retire B**, in the order that keeps every step safe -- from A's checkout,
since B's is about to stop being one. Forget B's checkout, drop B's dataset
commit (which releases the pins only it referenced), delete the bookmark, and
let `gc` judge its branches: their heads were pinned by B's commit until the
abandon, so with the commit gone they hold writes no pin covers and are kept
unless you say otherwise.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="49%"}
```bash
tether forget-workspace 3e9b2c71
tether abandon b --gc
jj bookmark delete b             # git: git branch -D b
tether gc --prune-bookmarks --force-prune --no-dry-run
```

```
forgot workspace 3e9b2c71
  removed  /.../analysis-b/.tether/workspace.toml
  vcs      jj workspace 'analysis-b' forgotten (its directory is left in place)
abandoned c4d82f1a6e93
unpinned 2 pin(s)
  icechunk: 0a1b2c3d.9c3a...
  lance: 0a1b2c3d.71d4...
deleted 2 branch(es)
  deleted  zarr/imaging: tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.b  FORCED although it has unpinned writes
  deleted  features: tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.b  FORCED although it has unpinned writes
```
:::
::: {.column width="2%"}
:::
::: {.column width="49%"}
Nothing left to run here. The directory can be deleted (`git worktree
remove` already did, for git).

Without `--force-prune`, `gc` keeps the two branches and says so: B's writes
are on them and nothing else holds them. Delete the bookmark *before* the
abandon and `gc` sees pinned heads and deletes them without force -- the
abandon then only releases the pins.
:::
::::

```bash
jj log
```

```
@  ozxwmqtn e7b2c4a1 (empty) (no description set)
○  vmnzstyq 5a1e9c0d a main | Labels: candidate A
○  wknmqzlt 7f3a2c1d Metrics rewritten for model v3
○  kmpvtnwq 8d571984 Inputs for the Q3 report
◆  zzzzzzzz 00000000
```

B is gone from history, its pins from the stores, and its branches from
Icechunk and Lance. `a` and `main` point at the same commit; `jj bookmark
delete a` and a later `gc --prune-bookmarks` retire the winner's branches the
same way once nobody works on them.

Read next: [Branching and Writing](04-branching-and-writing.qmd#workspaces-and-bookmarks),
[Reclaiming Storage](05-reclaiming-storage.qmd).

## 4. Catch drift nightly without a watcher

*Twenty inputs across four systems. Some are "immutable" raw files. Something
will change under you eventually, and you would rather hear it from a cron job
than from a wrong result.*

Back on the trunk, register the inventory -- by hand, or from the registry
that already lists it -- and commit it:

```bash
tether new main
tether import inventory.csv       # key, kind, uri, ... one row per object
tether commit -m "Inventory as of 2026-09-01"
```

```bash
jj log
```

```
@  hrnpqvxs 0c7e5d3a (empty) (no description set)
○  nsxkopmv 2b9e4d10 main | Inventory as of 2026-09-01
○  vmnzstyq 5a1e9c0d a | Labels: candidate A
○  wknmqzlt 7f3a2c1d Metrics rewritten for model v3
○  kmpvtnwq 8d571984 Inputs for the Q3 report
◆  zzzzzzzz 00000000
```

Then schedule two commands:

```bash
tether status --snapshot   # fingerprints every object concurrently; exit 1 if an immutable file changed
tether verify          # exit 1 if a pin is missing or points elsewhere
```

(`status --snapshot` only *reports*; nothing moves. Run it on the trunk:
`modified` means an upstream branch moved, `behind` that a branch-less
object's system has a newer state than the pin -- `tether pull` commits both
when you want them.)

A raw file overwritten in place -- its bytes, not its timestamp (`status`
stops at the snapshot; the exit code is 1):

```
error: immutable object 'raw/plate1' changed since it was committed; re-register with acceptance to record the new state
```

A tag moved by hand in the Icechunk repo, so it no longer names what the
manifest says:

```
      ok  db/metrics  
 drifted  zarr/imaging  tether.0a1b2c3d.6674305d5e1fe5f6 -> K9B2M1A7C3D8E4F0, expected 6674305D5E1FQ2ZJ
```

Nothing watches anything. Each run fingerprints the objects (an Icechunk
snapshot id, a Neon LSN, a Lance version, one `LIST` of the prefix) and
compares them with the manifests; the cost is one round of metadata calls.
Neither command touches history. A third one does, when you want the dataset
to *trail* the world rather than merely watch it: a nightly `tether pull` on
`main` commits whatever moved, and leaves nothing when nothing did.

```bash
tether pull
```

```
  pulled db/metrics  lsn=0/1A2B3C4D -> lsn=0/1B0000F8
  pulled raw/plate2  digest=9f2e1c… -> digest=0b7a4d…
  up to date zarr/imaging
  up to date features
  up to date code
committed 66a1b2c3d4e5 on main
```

```bash
jj log
```

```
@  gkvsxwmp 5e2a1b9c (empty) (no description set)
○  tpywqzlo 66a1b2c3 main | pull main: 2 objects
○  nsxkopmv 2b9e4d10 Inventory as of 2026-09-01
○  vmnzstyq 5a1e9c0d a | Labels: candidate A
○  wknmqzlt 7f3a2c1d Metrics rewritten for model v3
○  kmpvtnwq 8d571984 Inputs for the Q3 report
◆  zzzzzzzz 00000000
```

Read next: [Pinning](03-pinning.qmd#drift), [Registries and SQL](10-registries-and-sql.qmd).

## 5. Keep the data bill down

*Two weeks of experiments, five commits a day, each pinning a snapshot the
store must now keep. Only the last one matters.*

Decide at `add` time which objects deserve durable pins, and run the sweep on
its own bookmark:

```bash
tether add scratch/features --kind iceberg db.scratch_features --pin record   # no tag; the recorded snapshot lives as long as the table's retention
tether new -b sweep
python sweep.py --trial 1 && tether commit -m "sweep: trial 1"
python sweep.py --trial 2 && tether commit -m "sweep: trial 2"
python sweep.py --trial 3 && tether commit -m "sweep: trial 3"
python sweep.py --trial 4 && tether commit -m "sweep: trial 4"
```

```bash
jj log -r 'main::@'
```

```
@  yqtmxrwo 91d0a3e7 (empty) (no description set)
○  snyqvxop dd04f1a9 sweep | sweep: trial 4
○  krlwtmzy cc03e8b2 sweep: trial 3
○  ptnwqsyu bb02d7c1 sweep: trial 2
○  ulmxrkzt aa01c6d0 sweep: trial 1
○  tpywqzlo 66a1b2c3 main | pull main: 2 objects
~
```

When the experiment is over, drop the commits that were only tries and see
what that frees, in one step. Later commits keep their manifests exactly as
they were (they are snapshots, not patches), so trial 4 still names its own
pins:

```bash
tether abandon ptnwqsyu krlwtmzy --gc
```

```
abandoned bb02d7c1e9f0, cc03e8b2a7d6
unpinned 4 pin(s)
  icechunk: 0a1b2c3d.7d1e0c9a2b34e5f6
  icechunk: 0a1b2c3d.c48b2f6e1d07a9b0
  lance: 0a1b2c3d.7d1e0c9a2b34e5f6
  lance: 0a1b2c3d.c48b2f6e1d07a9b0
```

```bash
jj log -r 'main::@'
```

```
@  yqtmxrwo 4b8e2f01 (empty) (no description set)
○  snyqvxop ee05a0c3 sweep | sweep: trial 4
○  ulmxrkzt aa01c6d0 sweep: trial 1
○  tpywqzlo 66a1b2c3 main | pull main: 2 objects
~
```

Trial 4 was rebased onto trial 1 (new commit id, same change id, same
manifests), the `sweep` bookmark followed it, and `scratch/features` freed
nothing -- it had no pins to release, which was the point of `--pin record`.
Releasing a tag makes the snapshot *eligible*; the store reclaims the bytes on
its own schedule (`repo.expire_snapshots(...)` then `repo.garbage_collect(...)`
for Icechunk, `cleanup_old_versions()` for Lance). Recorded states past their
retention show up in `tether verify --all-history` as missing -- that is the
trade you made with `--pin record`, stated back to you.

Read next: [Reclaiming Storage](05-reclaiming-storage.qmd).

## 6. Recover

*Something went wrong. Three kinds of wrong, and what comes back.*

**An unwanted `new`** -- you started a bookmark you did not mean to and forked
into it. The op log knows what was created:

```bash
tether new -b scratch --eager
tether ops
tether undo
```

```
undid 3f1c9a2b7d4e (new: forked db/metrics, zarr/imaging; on scratch)
  restored   db/metrics: deleted tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.scratch
  restored   zarr/imaging: deleted tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.scratch
  restored   workspace.toml restored
  restored   bookmark scratch deleted
```

**One object's branch on the wrong state** -- everything else is fine, only
`zarr/imaging` should go back to what an older commit pinned:

```bash
tether restore zarr/imaging --from 8d5719841a09
```

The other branches, the manifests, and the working copy stay put; the next
`commit` pins what you restored. (Here it was a demonstration, so `tether
undo` puts the `sweep` branch back to trial 4's head before we go on.)

**A pin deleted by hand, or by a `gc` run on the wrong clone** -- the
manifests still promise it:

```bash
tether verify              # drifted / missing
tether repair              # recreate every missing pin from its recorded state, while the store still has it
```

```
repinned  zarr/imaging -> 0a1b2c3d.6674305d5e1fe5f6
```

And when several things went wrong in a row, `tether undo --to <op id>` walks
back through every operation newer than that one, stopping -- with everything
so far reversed -- at the first the store will not allow.

None of this touched history: the `scratch` bookmark came and went without a
commit, and `restore` and `repair` act on the stores. The log is what section
5 left, and the workspace is back on `sweep`:

```bash
jj log -r 'main::@'
```

```
@  yqtmxrwo 4b8e2f01 (empty) (no description set)
○  snyqvxop ee05a0c3 sweep | sweep: trial 4
○  ulmxrkzt aa01c6d0 sweep: trial 1
○  tpywqzlo 66a1b2c3 main | pull main: 2 objects
~
```

The boundary: `jj undo` and `git reset` move the manifests, never the stores;
tether's `undo` and `repair` cover tether's side and say exactly what they
could not do (a pin whose snapshot the store already expired, a `promote`).
`status` also tells you when a dataset commit vanished from the VCS behind
tether's back, or a bookmark was deleted, renamed, or moved by hand.

Read next: [CLI Guide](07-cli.qmd#ops-undo-repair), [Concepts](02-concepts.qmd#the-operation-log).

## 7. Publish history to a registry (experimental)

*A dashboard, a training pipeline, and a data catalog all want to know which
state of which table a run used. None of them should have to clone the
repository to find out.*

Land the sweep first, then push the history into Postgres -- after every
`promote` to `main`, typically from CI:

```bash
tether promote                                   # sweep -> main (fast-forwards; main moves)
tether publish --to "$REGISTRY_DSN" --schema tether
```

```
published 41 row(s) to schema 'tether' (0 commit(s) already present)
  commits               7 row(s)
  commit_parents        6 row(s)
  objects              22 row(s)
  object_states        16 row(s)
```

Consumers join their own run log against `tether.object_states`:

```sql
select r.run_id, s.key, s.pin_id, s.state_json
from   runs r
join   tether.object_states s on s.commit_id = r.dataset_commit
where  r.run_id = 'train-2026-09-14';
```

For a provenance dashboard, `tether export ./history --format parquet` writes
the same tables as files. And when the registry -- not the repository -- is
where objects are declared, run the other direction: `tether import` from a
query, `commit`, and the manifests follow the registry.

Producers and consumers meet in the middle: the producer commits and
publishes, the consumer's pipeline runs `tether verify --rev <commit>` before
training and refuses to start on a pin that is gone.

`publish` writes to Postgres, not to the repository; only the `promote` moved
anything here. The story ends with every line of work landed on `main`:

```bash
jj log
```

```
@  yqtmxrwo 4b8e2f01 (empty) (no description set)
○  snyqvxop ee05a0c3 main sweep | sweep: trial 4
○  ulmxrkzt aa01c6d0 sweep: trial 1
○  tpywqzlo 66a1b2c3 pull main: 2 objects
○  nsxkopmv 2b9e4d10 Inventory as of 2026-09-01
○  vmnzstyq 5a1e9c0d a | Labels: candidate A
○  wknmqzlt 7f3a2c1d Metrics rewritten for model v3
○  kmpvtnwq 8d571984 Inputs for the Q3 report
◆  zzzzzzzz 00000000
```

Read next: [Registries and SQL](10-registries-and-sql.qmd).
